subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: At the Talk boundary the demo renders the kit's Presentation with title, steps and initialMode. At the shared Scene boundary, Diagram builds on the kit's SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis. It passes each entity's catalog id as the node's id, and the kit nodes forward that to layoutId. It uses the kit's previous-payload prop to decide Appear wrapping. It does not re-implement layout, motion or stage mechanics. Whether groupKey is used is scored under the grouping criterion, not here.
evidence: Talk.tsx imports Presentation from '../../presentation-kit' and renders <Presentation title=... steps={STEPS} initialMode="browse" />.
scene.tsx Diagram({payload, previous}: SceneProps<DiagramState>) returns <SceneLayer> and wraps new ids in <Appear>, leaving continuing ids unwrapped in a Fragment.
scene.tsx renderEntity maps each entity kind to kit Box/Label/SymbolChip/Arrow/Frame/Emphasis, passing id={id}.
nodes/Box.tsx and nodes/Arrow.tsx set layoutId={id} on a motion.div with layout.
Every step module sets Scene: Diagram, which is the shared kit-typed SceneProps component.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Stable entity identity is met. Presentation-owned EntityId and ENTITIES keys flow through Diagram's renderEntity as id into the kit nodes, which set layoutId={id}. All nineteen-plus ids are used across the nine steps. The grouped-scene part is unmet. Stage derives the scene key from step.groupKey when it is set, and otherwise from `step:${step.id}`. None of the nine step modules sets groupKey, and a grep for groupKey in src finds only the type declaration and Stage. So every step gets a distinct sceneKey. Navigating between adjacent steps that use the same Diagram component mounts a separate scene and cross-fades it through AnimatePresence. It does not update one existing scene instance with the new step state. The guidance says a single groupKey shared by all nine steps is the correct grouping for this continuously evolving scene, and the delivered deck has none.
evidence: Stage.tsx line 42: sceneKey = `${step.groupKey ? `group:${step.groupKey}` : `step:${step.id}`}:scene${sceneId(Scene)}` and the motion.div uses key={sceneKey}.
Steps 01-09 each export a Step with id, era, title, caption, Scene: Diagram and payload, and none has a groupKey field.
A grep of src for 'groupKey' returns only types.ts:16-17 and Stage.tsx:30,42, with no step or Talk usage.
Steps 01-09 give distinct ids ('you-have-a-topic' through 'youre-looking-at-one'), so each falls back to its own `step:<id>` key.
entities.ts ENTITIES/EntityId, scene.tsx renderEntity (id={id}) and Box.tsx/Arrow.tsx (layoutId={id}) show identity is carried correctly.
judging basis: consensus-fail

The presentations registry only maps slug, title and lazy load. The public title contract is consumed: Presentation passes title as deckTitle to Header, which renders it in browse mode. The shared constants I traced (MIN_SCALE, SWIPE_MIN_PX, DEFAULT_MODE, ENTER_T, ENTER_DELAY, DESIGN_W/H) are each consumed in the kit. Every ENTITIES member appears in the step payloads, the last of which lists all of them, and is rendered with id/layoutId, so no dead entity constants were found.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Every entity primitive sets `layout` and `layoutId={id}` with a LAYOUT_TRANSITION layout transition. Stage wraps scenes in a LayoutGroup. An entity with the same id therefore animates from its old geometry to its new one.
evidence: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip each render motion.div with `layout`, `transition={{ layout: LAYOUT_TRANSITION }}` and `layoutId={id}`.
Entity geometry is applied through inline left/top/width/height, so layout projection animates position and size.
Stage.tsx wraps scenes in `<LayoutGroup>`.
layout-id.test.tsx asserts layoutId, layout true and LAYOUT_T for every primitive.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: For ungrouped steps, Stage uses AnimatePresence in default sync mode. The outgoing scene is taken out of flow and the incoming scene mounts at once. Continuing entities are not hidden, so the shared layoutId can morph.
evidence: Stage.tsx: `<AnimatePresence>` without mode="wait". The scene motion.div is `position: absolute; inset: 0`, has only `exit={{opacity: 0}}` and no initial opacity.
Scene.tsx Diagram renders continuing entities unwrapped (no initial opacity 0) as `<Fragment key={id}>{node}</Fragment>`, so the incoming copy is visible immediately.
The primitives have no initial opacity and no entry delay on their layout animation.
stage.test.tsx 'a continuing entity is rendered in both steps...' asserts two copies of `shared` are mounted together after Next.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: Newcomers get a fade-in with a 0.7s delay, longer than the 0.6s layout transition. The delay is applied only to the Appear wrapper, not to the continuing entities' layout motion. Every newly introduced sample entity goes through Appear.
evidence: constants.ts: LAYOUT_T = 0.6, LAYOUT_TRANSITION duration 0.6, ENTER_DELAY = 0.7, ENTER_T = 0.5.
Appear.tsx: `initial={{opacity:0}} animate={{opacity:1}} transition={{delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T}}`.
The continuing path (Box etc.) uses `transition={{ layout: LAYOUT_TRANSITION }}` with no delay.
scene.tsx Diagram wraps every id not in `previous.visible` in `<Appear>` and leaves continuing ids unwrapped. This covers all sample entity kinds.
appear.test.tsx asserts delay >= LAYOUT_T. sample-motion.test.tsx asserts wrappers start at opacity 0. layout-id.test.tsx asserts the forward and backward wrapping classification.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: SceneLayer wraps its children in AnimatePresence and every primitive declares `exit={EXIT}`, so departing entities stay rendered while they fade out. The sample renders all its entities through SceneLayer and these primitives.
evidence: SceneLayer.tsx: `<AnimatePresence>{children}</AnimatePresence>` over keyed direct children.
Primitives set `exit={EXIT}` (opacity 0 over LAYOUT_T).
scene.tsx Diagram renders every entity inside `<SceneLayer>` using Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis.
stage.test.tsx 'a departing entity stays mounted through its exit, then is removed' covers this.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: Stage derives the scene key from the groupKey and the Scene identity, so adjacent steps with the same group and Scene keep one mounted instance. Only the payload changes.
evidence: Stage.tsx: `sceneKey = group:${groupKey}` or `step:${id}`, plus `:scene${sceneId(Scene)}`. Steps with the same group and Scene share a key and one motion.div.

judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The grouped scene instance stays mounted. The kit's Diagram scene renders continuing entities without the newcomer Appear wrapper, so they morph through layoutId projection.
evidence: Stage.tsx keeps the same keyed scene element for a shared groupKey and Scene, so state persists and nothing replays.
scene.tsx: ids in `previous.visible` render as `<Fragment key={id}>{node}</Fragment>`, with no Appear and no initial opacity. Only new ids are wrapped.

judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: Entities are placed with literal absolute geometry and the kit does not auto-layout or de-overlap them. The sample's overlapping and stacked compositions are kept while the primitives still morph via layoutId.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: A single fit factor is applied to both axes. It is computed from the stage element's actual rendered box and recomputed on resize, so the fixed-size canvas scales without internal reflow.
evidence: useFitScale.computeFitScale returns one value, `Math.max(MIN_SCALE, Math.min(usableW / width, usableH / height))`. The input is the stage element's getBoundingClientRect.
Stage.tsx applies it as `transform: translate(-50%,-50%) scale(${scale})` on a canvas fixed at geometry.width × geometry.height, with the stage `overflow: hidden`.
useFitScale re-measures on window resize and when the per-mode geometry changes.
At 390×844 the width limit is (390−32)/880 ≈ 0.41, above MIN_SCALE 0.3. At 1280×720 the stage is the measured flex:1 area, so the height-limited scale stays within it.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: index.ts exports eight public scene primitives: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. All three clauses are met for each. 1. None uses an untyped bag. The six node primitives declare typed interfaces that extend DataProps, which is the template-literal type { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined } and not Record<string, unknown>. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. 2. Identity hooks come after caller props. Each node primitive spreads {...data} first on motion.div, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id. Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow sets data-presentation-two-way. Callers cannot override any of these. 3. Kit-only props stay off the DOM. id, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out, so the spread rest holds only data-* attributes. The guidance says typed primitives that apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because BoxProps is not the full motion.div prop type. The guidance's fail condition is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, and DataProps plus explicit typed fields is not one, so C's observation does not decide the requirement.

criteria.rationale: No delivered test opens Playwright itself. A search of tests/ for chromium, playwright, waitForTimeout and sleep finds only a 'playwright' dependency-name string in scaffold.test.ts. The browser-driving tests run the delivered verify and inspect scripts as subprocesses through helpers.run, which uses spawnSync. spawnSync blocks until the process exits, so the tests assert on finished output, not after a sleep. Inside the scripts, the step-advance and step-assert waits poll observable state. In verify, waitForIndex polls data-step-index every 50 ms up to STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, and the per-step title and caption are read only after that poll succeeds. In inspect, page.waitForFunction auto-waits until data-step-index equals the target step. Capture is then gated on waitUntilStable, which polls entity geometry until it stops changing. The only timer in the test code is E2E-002's waitFor helper, a deadline-bounded 100 ms poll on a predicate (preview process alive, 'preview ready at' in output, or process gone). That is a polling wait on observable state, not a fixed sleep. Judges A and B match this. Judge C points to `page.waitForTimeout(options.settle)` in inspect, but that does not decide the criterion. That delay is the helper's user-configurable settle interval, which the INT-002 test checks is honored. It runs only after waitForFunction has already confirmed the step index, so it is not a fixed wait before asserting the step. The capture is still gated by geometry-stability polling. INT-002 also shows a `--settle 0` capture is byte-identical to the default capture, so correctness rests on the state polls, not on the delay. No test sleeps for a fixed time in place of waiting for state.

votes.rationale: At the Talk boundary the demo renders the kit's Presentation with title, steps and initialMode. At the shared Scene boundary, Diagram builds on the kit's SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis. It passes each entity's catalog id as the node's id, and the kit nodes forward that to layoutId. It uses the kit's previous-payload prop to decide Appear wrapping. It does not re-implement layout, motion or stage mechanics. Whether groupKey is used is scored under the grouping criterion, not here.
evidence: Talk.tsx imports Presentation from '../../presentation-kit' and renders <Presentation title=... steps={STEPS} initialMode="browse" />.

scene.tsx renderEntity maps each entity kind to kit Box/Label/SymbolChip/Arrow/Frame/Emphasis, passing id={id}.
nodes/Box.tsx and nodes/Arrow.tsx set layoutId={id} on a motion.div with layout.

votes.rationale: Stable entity identity is met. Presentation-owned EntityId and ENTITIES keys flow through Diagram's renderEntity as id into the kit nodes, which set layoutId={id}. All nineteen-plus ids are used across the nine steps. The grouped-scene part is unmet. Stage derives the scene key from step.groupKey when it is set, and otherwise from `step:${step.id}`. None of the nine step modules sets groupKey, and a grep for groupKey in src finds only the type declaration and Stage. So every step gets a distinct sceneKey. Navigating between adjacent steps that use the same Diagram component mounts a separate scene and cross-fades it through AnimatePresence. It does not update one existing scene instance with the new step state. The guidance says a single groupKey shared by all nine steps is the correct grouping for this continuously evolving scene, and the delivered deck has none.
evidence: Stage.tsx line 42: sceneKey = `${step.groupKey ? `group:${step.groupKey}` : `step:${step.id}`}:scene${sceneId(Scene)}` and the motion.div uses key={sceneKey}.
Steps 01-09 each export a Step with id, era, title, caption, Scene: Diagram and payload, and none has a groupKey field.
A grep of src for 'groupKey' returns only types.ts:16-17 and Stage.tsx:30,42, with no step or Talk usage.
Steps 01-09 give distinct ids ('you-have-a-topic' through 'youre-looking-at-one'), so each falls back to its own `step:<id>` key.
entities.ts ENTITIES/EntityId, scene.tsx renderEntity (id={id}) and Box.tsx/Arrow.tsx (layoutId={id}) show identity is carried correctly.

votes.rationale: Stable entity identity is in place. The ENTITIES catalog supplies the ids, Diagram passes them as id to the kit nodes, and Box and Arrow forward them as layoutId. votes.rationale: Readiness in startPreview() comes from HTTP polling (fetch of `${url}/`), not from the child's own announcement of its address. The only ownership check is `if (exited)`, evaluated once at the top of each loop iteration before the request. The port comes from findFreePort(), which binds, closes and releases it, so another process can take it before vite starts. A server on that port could then answer the probe before the child's exit is observed. --strictPort alone does not prevent this. Neither accepted mechanism is present: there is no readiness parsed from the child's output, and the poll is not raced against the child's exit.

child stdout/stderr are only collected into outputTail for error messages and never parsed for readiness

votes.rationale: The kit index exports eight public primitives: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. I checked each one. None types its props as an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>. Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip declare named interfaces with explicit field types. They extend DataProps, which is the template-literal index signature { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined }, so extra pass-through props are limited to typed data-* attributes. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. This is typed, but it is narrower than the full rendered-element props: the primitives do not accept aria-* or event props. I treated that as a design choice, since the requirement fails an untyped bag and these are not one. On identity hooks, each of the six node primitives spreads {...data} first on the motion.div. After that spread they set layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id; Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow data-presentation-two-way. A caller's data-presentation-* value therefore cannot override them. Appear and SceneLayer spread no caller props, and their data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-layer hooks are fixed. On kit-only props, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out of the props. The rest object contains only data-* attributes, so none of them reaches the DOM. The repo src/presentation-kit copies match the bootstrap copies: the grep shows the same ...data destructuring and the same layoutId ordering.

A search of tests/ for chromium, playwright, waitForTimeout and sleep finds only a 'playwright' dependency-name string in scaffold.test.ts. The browser-driving tests run the delivered verify and inspect scripts as subprocesses through helpers.run, which uses spawnSync. spawnSync blocks until the process exits, so the tests assert on finished output, not after a sleep. Inside the scripts, the step-advance and step-assert waits poll observable state. In verify, waitForIndex polls data-step-index every 50 ms up to STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, and the per-step title and caption are read only after that poll succeeds. In inspect, page.waitForFunction auto-waits until data-step-index equals the target step. Capture is then gated on waitUntilStable, which polls entity geometry until it stops changing. The only timer in the test code is E2E-002's waitFor helper, a deadline-bounded 100 ms poll on a predicate (preview process alive, 'preview ready at' in output, or process gone). That is a polling wait on observable state, not a fixed sleep. Judges A and B match this. Judge C points to `page.waitForTimeout(options.settle)` in inspect, but that does not decide the criterion. That delay is the helper's user-configurable settle interval, which the INT-002 test checks is honored. It runs only after waitForFunction has already confirmed the step index, so it is not a fixed wait before asserting the step. The capture is still gated by geometry-stability polling. INT-002 also shows a `--settle 0` capture is byte-identical to the default capture, so correctness rests on the state polls, not on the delay. No test sleeps for a fixed time in place of waiting for state.

scene-kit.rationale: computeFitScale returns one factor, min(usableW/width, usableH/height), floored at MIN_SCALE. It is applied as a single scale() transform on a fixed-size canvas. The input is the stage element's own measured rect (flex:1, overflow hidden), so the fit follows the area the stage actually occupies, and it is re-measured on resize. At 390×844 the width-limited scale is about 0.41, above the floor, so the 880-wide canvas fits within the 390px stage. At 1280×720 the scale is derived from the measured stage height, so it stays within it. The packet shows no reference-viewport counterexample.

scene-kit.rationale: Every kit primitive renders a motion.div with layout, layoutId={id} and a layout transition. Stage wraps the scene in a LayoutGroup. The sample uses each entity id as the primitive's id. A same-id entity across consecutive steps therefore animates in place.

scene-kit.rationale: Ungrouped steps get different scene keys. Stage uses AnimatePresence in its default sync mode, so the outgoing scene stays mounted. The outgoing scene is position:absolute and out of layout flow. The incoming scene wrapper has no initial opacity. Continuing entities are unwrapped, so they carry no opacity-0 start or entrance delay. They stay visible and morph by layoutId.
evidence: Stage.tsx: keyed motion.div, position absolute, inset 0, exit={{opacity:0}}, no initial.
scene.tsx: ids in the previous payload render in a plain Fragment, not Appear.
Primitives apply the delay-free LAYOUT_TRANSITION to layout only.

scene-kit.rationale: ENTER_DELAY (0.7 s) is at least LAYOUT_T (0.6 s). The delay is set only on Appear's opacity transition. The layout path uses LAYOUT_TRANSITION with no delay. Diagram wraps every id not in the previous payload in Appear, so no step-introduced entity renders without entry motion. The Appear wrapper starts at opacity 0, so the newcomer's visible entry begins after the layout motion ends.
evidence: constants.ts: LAYOUT_T = 0.6, ENTER_DELAY = 0.7.
Appear.tsx: initial opacity 0, animate opacity 1, transition delay ENTER_DELAY.

geometry.test.tsx asserts ENTER_DELAY >= LAYOUT_T; sample-motion.test.tsx asserts newcomer wrappers start at opacity 0.

scene-kit.rationale: All primitives set exit={EXIT}, a fade over LAYOUT_T. SceneLayer wraps children in AnimatePresence, so departing entities stay mounted while they animate out. scene-kit.rationale: useFitScale measures the stage element's own bounding rect (the flex area left between header and footer), not the window. computeFitScale takes min(usableW/width, usableH/height) after subtracting the mode padding, giving one factor. Stage applies it as a single scale() on a fixed-size canvas, centered inside an overflow-hidden stage. The scale is recomputed on window resize and on mode change. At the reference viewports the stage area is measured directly, so the canvas fits it. The unpadded fit at 390 wide is about 0.41, above the 0.3 floor, so the floor does not take effect. No source arithmetic shows the canvas outside the stage.
evidence: useFitScale.ts: element.getBoundingClientRect() → computeFitScale; fit = Math.min(usableW/width, usableH/height).
Stage.tsx: transform translate(-50%,-50%) scale(${scale}); stage is flex:1, minHeight:0, overflow:hidden.
geometry.test.tsx covers computeFitScale, recompute on resize and the single uniform transform.

votes.rationale: Readiness in startPreview() comes from HTTP polling (fetch of `${url}/`), not from the child's own announcement of its address. The only ownership check is `if (exited)`, evaluated once at the top of each loop iteration before the request. The port comes from findFreePort(), which binds, closes and releases it, so another process can take it before vite starts. A server on that port could then answer the probe before the child's exit is observed. --strictPort alone does not prevent this. Neither accepted mechanism is present: there is no readiness parsed from the child's output, and the poll is not raced against the child's exit.

votes.rationale: The kit index exports eight public primitives: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. I checked each one. None types its props as an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>. Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip declare named interfaces with explicit field types. They extend DataProps, which is the template-literal index signature { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined }, so extra pass-through props are limited to typed data-* attributes. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. This is typed, but it is narrower than the full rendered-element props: the primitives do not accept aria-* or event props. I treated that as a design choice, since the requirement fails an untyped bag and these are not one. On identity hooks, each of the six node primitives spreads {...data} first on the motion.div. After that spread they set layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id; Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow data-presentation-two-way. A caller's data-presentation-* value therefore cannot override them. Appear and SceneLayer spread no caller props, and their data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-layer hooks are fixed. On kit-only props, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out of the props. The rest object contains only data-* attributes, so none of them reaches the DOM. The repo src/presentation-kit copies match the bootstrap copies: the grep shows the same ...data destructuring and the same layoutId ordering.

first_results.rationale: All three clauses are met. 1. Every preview-readiness wait is bounded. startPreview in both the repo and bootstrap preview.mjs loops only while Date.now() < deadline, where the deadline is now + READY_TIMEOUT_MS (30 000 ms). After the deadline it stops the process group and throws. 2. The preview starts only after the build finishes. verify.mjs awaits runBuild(root, log) before it calls startPreview. runBuild resolves only on the build child's exit with code 0. inspect also awaits runBuild before startPreview; with --skip-build it runs no build at all, so no build is running while the preview starts. 3. The ready-URL clause does not apply. Readiness is an HTTP fetch probe, and the printed output is only kept as a tail for error messages. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C's reason is that the awaited fetch has no abort signal. The criterion asks for a timeout on every readiness wait, and this wait loop has a hard deadline with cleanup. C's case needs a server that accepts the connection and never answers, which is a hypothetical that neither the requirement nor the guidance names. It does not show the readiness wait is unbounded for the behaviour the candidate produces.

first_results.rationale: index.ts exports eight public scene primitives: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. All three clauses are met for each. 1. None uses an untyped bag. The six node primitives declare typed interfaces that extend DataProps, which is the template-literal type { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined } and not Record<string, unknown>. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. 2. Identity hooks come after caller props. Each node primitive spreads {...data} first on motion.div, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id. Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow sets data-presentation-two-way. Callers cannot override any of these. 3. Kit-only props stay off the DOM. id, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out, so the spread rest holds only data-* attributes. The guidance says typed primitives that apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because BoxProps is not the full motion.div prop type. The guidance's fail condition is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, and DataProps plus explicit typed fields is not one, so C's observation does not decide the requirement.

first_results.rationale: No delivered test drives Playwright directly. Browser runs happen only through verify or inspect subprocesses, which tests launch with run() or spawn and then assert on exit status and output. The one in-test wait is E2E-002's waitFor helper. It polls a predicate on observable state (a preview process exists, or the output contains 'preview ready at') every 100 ms until a deadline, so it is not a fixed sleep. No test calls waitForTimeout or sleep. Inside inspect, the browser waits on state before capturing: waitForFunction polls data-step-index, then waitUntilStable polls entity geometry. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because INT-002 calls inspect with --settle 1500 and inspect runs page.waitForTimeout(options.settle). That settle interval is a configurable inspect-script option. The INT-002 test is checking that the option is honoured ('configured settle 1500ms', waited >= 1500), not sleeping in place of a state wait. In the script it also comes after the step-index wait. It is not a test sleeping for a transition before asserting the step, so it does not decide the requirement.
